title: Binding of a Macrocyclic Nonapeptide Inhibitor to Histone Deacetylase 6
abstract: Histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6) plays an essential role in the regulation of post-translational lysine acetylation. Myriad biological processes depend on the precise regulation of lysine acetylation-deacetylation cycles, and their dysregulation is linked to human pathologies such as cancer and neurodegeneration. Broad-specificity HDAC inhibitors are efficacious in treating disease, but the inhibitors currently approved for clinical use often cause deleterious side effects due to inhibition of multiple HDAC isozymes as well as other zinc enzymes. Cyclic peptides comprise novel platforms that, in principle, can be tailored for affinity and selectivity. A key advantage of cyclic peptide design is the ability to incorporate both canonical and noncanonical amino acids. As part of our program focusing on cyclic peptide HDAC inhibitors, we now report the 1.9-[A] resolution crystal structure of HDAC6 CD2 complexed with macrocyclic nonapeptide 1. The structure reveals zinc coordination by a noncanonical thiolate-containing amino acid, plus direct and water-mediated enzyme-inhibitor hydrogen bonds that contribute to nanomolar inhibitory potency. Structural comparisons with previously reported HDAC6 CD2 complexes with tetrapeptide and octapeptide macrocycles reveal similar networks of direct and water-mediated interactions. Given the surge of interest in cyclic peptide inhibitors, fueled in part by advances in computational design approaches, the crystal structure of the HDAC6 CD2-1 complex sets an important foundation for further development of macrocyclic peptide inhibitors.

title: Insulin fails to mitigate amyloid pathology but modulates intestinal morphology in the 5xFAD model revealed by synchrotron-based XPCT
abstract: Intranasal insulin has been investigated as a metabolic intervention in Alzheimers disease (AD), but its effects across the brain-gut axis remain unclear. We combined multiscale synchrotron X-ray phase-contrast tomography (XPCT), amyloid-{beta} immunofluorescence, and fecal metaproteomics to examine structural and molecular responses in 5xFAD mice. Twenty-four mice representing wild-type and 5xFAD genotypes, saline and insulin conditions, and terminal ages of 2 and 6 months received insulin at 1 U/mouse/day for 5 weeks.

title: From HPV infection to cervical precancer: Molecular mechanisms, immune microenvironment and emerging technologies
abstract: Cervical cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality among women globally, with persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) infection as the primary etiological factor. Cervical precancerous lesions, including high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions and adenocarcinoma in situ, represent the critical window for intervention prior to invasive cancer development. However, additional factors such as immunosuppression, smoking, and microbiome composition also play crucial roles in the development of cervical precancerous lesions. While HPV vaccination, screening, and treatment have reduced cancer incidence, these must be complemented by personalized approaches that target the molecular mechanisms driving carcinogenesis. Key dysregulated tumor suppressors (e.g., p16) and signaling pathways (PI3K/AKT/mTOR, Wnt/β-catenin) highlight the need for advanced therapeutic strategies. The immune microenvironment also plays a critical role in cancer progression, suggesting potential for immunotherapy. Promising biomarkers like p16, Ki67, and microRNAs require integration with technologies such as single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics for deeper insights into tumor heterogeneity and microenvironment dynamics. Additionally, while deep learning models hold promise in improving diagnostic accuracy for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN), challenges such as data variability and interpretability need addressing. In conclusion, incorporating genomics, transcriptomics, immunotherapy, and artificial intelligence will enable more personalized and effective interventions, ultimately reducing the global burden of cervical cancer.

title: Ortho-, meta- and para-substituted fluorescent probes based on BODIPY for detecting esterase with application in machine learning and bioimaging
abstract: Esterase plays a significant role in industrial production and life activities. The method of fluorescent probe is employed for detecting esterase due to their excellent performance. However, the restriction of recognition groups to specific positions severely limits the molecular design and performance optimization of fluorescent probe. Thus, three fluorescent probes (OBOD6, MBOD6 and PBOD6) based on BODIPY with recognition groups at ortho-, meta- and para- positions were designed and synthesized to systematically investigate the positional effects on performance of probes.

title: Development of a Novel Non-Invasive Blood Pressure Measurement Technique Using Near-Infrared Spectroscopy and Deep Neural Networks
abstract: Non-invasive monitoring of blood pressure is essential for health management in daily life, particularly for elderly individuals and patients with autonomic dysfunction. However, conventional cuff-based sphygmomanometers are uncomfortable and provide discontinuous monitoring. In this study, we propose a novel non-invasive technique for blood pressure change assessment based on prefrontal near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) and deep neural networks.

title: Permutationally Invariant Polynomial Descriptors as Colored Multigraphs
abstract: The combinatorial explosion in monomial counts limits the extension of global permutationally invariant polynomial (PIP) potential energy surfaces to larger molecular systems. We use graph-theoretic language to reformulate PIPs as colored multigraphs and develop a series of theoretical and computational tools. First, we introduce an offline PIP generation algorithm whose cost has an upper bound independent of atom count for a fixed degree cutoff and number of element types. Second, we introduce a new online PIP evaluation algorithm, termed tensor-network descent. For the full PIP set through degree $d$ in a system of $M$ atoms, the evaluation complexity for $1\le d\le14$ is $O\!\left(f(d)M^{\left\lfloor(\sqrt{1+8d}+1)/2\right\rfloor}\right)$. At the commonly used cutoff of $d=5$, the online evaluation complexity decreases from the $M^{10}$ scaling of conventional explicit term-by-term computation to $M^3$. Numerical tests using the full PIP set through degree 5 show that our method achieves speedups of several orders of magnitude on most MD17 systems and remains computationally affordable for systems containing more than one thousand atoms. The method has a native tensor form, supports automatic differentiation, and provides a unified theoretical construction of four classes of PIP descriptors defined consistently across systems---global, atom-centered, bond-centered, and cluster-centered---establishing a representation and computational foundation for PIP potentials for large systems and for transfer across systems. Together, these results show that PIPs are neither inherently restricted to small systems nor intrinsically nontransferable.

title: Diffusion-controlled reactions with time-dependent surface reactivity
abstract: We investigate diffusion-controlled reactions on a reactive surface with time-dependent reactivity. Starting from a conventional formulation via diffusion equation with Robin boundary condition for the macroscopic concentration of particles, we aim at quantifying how temporal variations of reactivity affect the survival probability and the associated first-reaction time (FRT) of a single particle on the reactive surface. Using an adiabatic description, we first identify five long-time regimes of the first-reaction time distribution, ranging from exponential and stretched-exponential to power-law decay. In particular, sufficiently rapid decay of the reactivity leads to a nonzero probability of never reacting, despite diffusion in a bounded domain. Second, we provide a probabilistic reformulation of this problem and compare it with a different scenario of encounter-dependent reactivity. Our theoretical predictions are validated via extensive Monte Carlo simulations.

title: Low-Cost Third-order Algebraic Diagrammatic Construction Method for Excited States Using Tensor Hypercontraction and State-Specific Frozen Natural Orbitals
abstract: We have developed a reduced-cost framework for excited-state calculations by combining the state-specific frozen natural orbital (SS-FNO) approach with the third-order algebraic diagrammatic construction [ADC(3)] method and tensor hypercontraction (THC). This strategy enables a systematic and controllable truncation of the virtual orbital space, while significantly lowering the computational scaling through the THC representation of the electron repulsion integrals. The method allows black-box application via adjustable thresholds and includes a perturbative correction that compensates for the truncation error. We have used the CIS(D) method to generate the natural orbitals for the excited states. The performance of the SS-FNO-THC-ADC(3) method is assessed for valence, Rydberg, and charge-transfer excitations. Benchmark calculations demonstrate that the combined approach achieves excellent agreement with the canonical ADC(3) results. The efficiency of the present implementation is demonstrated by calculating the excitation energy of a molecule containing 31 atoms and more than one thousand basis functions.

title: Density Functional Theory and Data-Driven Insights into Hydrogen Incorporation and Transport in Ternary ABO3 Perovskites
abstract: Hydrogen is a promising energy carrier due to its clean and versatile nature, offering opportunities for decarbonizing diverse sectors. Hydrogen utilization in many applications relies on identifying and understanding materials with exceptional hydrogen storage and transport properties. In this study, we conducted a comprehensive investigation of the thermodynamic and kinetic properties of hydrogenation reactions in ternary ABO3 perovskites using density functional theory (DFT) calculations and machine learning (ML) screening.

title: Interplay between high-entropy effects and the superionic transition in fluorite oxides: A liquid-like perspective
abstract: Minor actinide (MA)-bearing mixed oxide (MOX), a prominent high-entropy ceramic (HEC), is a promising candidate for advanced fast reactor fuels. Using a hybrid Monte Carlo/Molecular Dynamics (MC/MD) approach, we reveal that Np and Am segregation establishes a distinct short-range order (SRO) that induces severe lattice distortion. We uncover a competitive mechanism between localized high-entropy blocking effects and collective superionic dynamics, where the anionic kinetic and structural evolution within the 2000-2800 K range is partitioned and governed by the Tammann crossover temperature and superionic transition temperature. In the low-temperature regime, severe lattice distortions induced by the SRO structures create localized electrostatic and strain-coupled potential wells, which spatially confine the O-ions and lead to their sluggish diffusion. The system exhibits increased dynamical heterogeneity as thermal activation alleviates these structural constraints. Crucially, these localized traps spontaneously transform into a highly interconnected, string-like polyhedral topological network. Driven by the maximization of configurational entropy, this structural change creates low-viscosity transport pathways that trigger confinement-enhanced diffusion. Consequently, a dramatic kinetic inversion occurs, where the O-ion mobility of SRO model surpasses that of random solid solution (RSS) model via an entropy-driven compensation mechanism. Finally, through Gibbs free energy minimization and defect analysis, structural and thermodynamic origins of the superionic transition in HEC are elucidated. This study unveils how local chemical ordering regulates ion transport under extreme conditions, providing theoretical support for the design of high-performance nuclear fuels with both superior radiation tolerance and optimized mass transfer capabilities.

title: Programming the Nonlinear Optics of a Nanoporous Photonic Metamaterial by Confined Crystallization
abstract: A membrane traversed by a dense array of nanochannels acts as a photonic metamaterial: with channels far smaller than the wavelength of light, the optical response is set by the architecture rather than by the constituent materials. Here each nanochannel is turned into a nonlinear optical meta-atom by filling anodic aluminum oxide (AAO) with benzil (BZL), a noncentrosymmetric molecular crystal, and the crystallization pathway programs their orientation. In free-standing membranes every channel solidifies independently, the orientations remain uncorrelated, and the effective second-harmonic generation (SHG) response is nearly polarization isotropic; its magnitude follows a core - shell model in which an optically inactive interfacial layer of 2.6 nm reduces the active volume of each meta-atom, reproducing on bare alumina the value previously found on alkyl-grafted silica and indicating a host-insensitive limit. Seeding crystallization from a bulk benzil layer instead aligns the meta-atoms over submillimeter domains and produces a macroscopically anisotropic effective susceptibility. Channel diameters from 32 to 270 nm span the transition out of the subwavelength regime, and the anomalous directional SHG emission reported here is confined to the metamaterial limit. Confined crystallization thus offers a route to nonlinear optical metamaterials whose effective susceptibility tensor is written during processing.

title: Adaptive Crack-Tip Localization of Phase-Field Fracture Computations
abstract: Phase-field models of fracture provide a unified framework for simulating crack nucleation and propagation, but their computational cost remains high because the governing equilibrium and phase-field equations are typically iteratively solved over the entire domain at every staggered iteration. We present an extension of the recently developed adaptive mesh refinement and coarsening framework that localizes not only spatial resolution but also repeated solution effort to a small active patch around the crack tip for linear elastic brittle materials. The inactive exterior is eliminated through a Schur complement and condensed onto the patch interface, and its factorization is reused as long as the patch remains fixed. The phase field is frozen in the exterior, introducing only a small approximation in the crack wake. The method is implemented in FEniCSx and evaluated for quasi-static crack propagation, dynamic crack branching, three-dimensional mixed-mode crack growth, and coalescence of multiple cracks in a unit cell. Across these problems, the condensed formulation reproduces the reference solutions with differences in global quantities below 0.5%, while substantially reducing the number of active degrees of freedom. In the quasi-static surfing problem, wall time speedups increase from 6.9 to 22.8 as the domain size is doubled, demonstrating increasing computational advantage for large-scale phase-field fracture simulations.

title: Cu–N3 Single-Atom Catalysts Enable High-Turnover C–N and C–O Cross-Coupling of Aryl Electrophiles
abstract: Transition-metal-catalyzed C–N cross-coupling is fundamental to the synthesis of pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and functional materials. However, many copper-based catalytic systems rely on exogenous molecular ligands to establish and tune the coordination environment around copper centers, which can increase catalyst-design complexity and complicate catalyst recovery and reuse.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: From Surface Reactions to Inhibitor Coverage: A Machine-Learning-Assisted Computational Study of Area-Selective Atomic Layer Deposition
abstract: Area-selective atomic layer deposition (AS-ALD) enables selective material growth for the fabrication of nanoscale semiconductor devices. Predicting inhibitor coverage is essential for understanding and optimizing surface blocking in AS-ALD. Here, we present a computational workflow combining a pretrained universal machine-learning interatomic potential with off-lattice grand canonical Monte Carlo simulations and apply it to inhibitor adsorption and precursor blocking on amorphous SiO2. Realistic surface models reveal substantial site-dependent variations in reaction energies and activation barriers, with silanol groups serving as the primary adsorption sites for aminosilane and related inhibitors and metal precursors. Coverage simulations show that inhibitors producing identical adsorbed fragments can yield different coverages because the intact molecules impose distinct steric constraints, leading to different accessible site densities and blocking capabilities. Beyond coverage, we highlight the importance of the reactivity of adsorbed inhibitor fragments toward precursors in determining inhibitor stability and blocking performance. Together, these findings demonstrate the need to consider both steric effects and chemical reactivity on realistic amorphous surfaces. Our calculations connect local reaction chemistry with inhibitor coverage and provide a computational basis for understanding inhibition mechanisms and selecting suitable inhibitor-precursor combinations for AS-ALD.

title: Scalable Levenberg-Marquardt Training Framework for Deep Learning
abstract: The Levenberg-Marquardt (LMA) algorithm is a widely used nonlinear least-squares solver known for its rapid convergence. For small-scale neural networks, LMA provides better convergence and architectural robustness than first-order optimizers like Adam. However, LMA imposes prohibitive memory and computational costs. These costs are primarily from the Jacobian matrix, whose dimensions scale with both the number of samples and parameters. This bottleneck prevents its use in large-scale neural networks. Recent efforts scale LMA using preconditioned conjugate gradient (PCG) solvers to avoid materializing the Jacobian. However, PCG only approximates the solution, requiring many network propagations and a task-specific preconditioner. Other studies optimize LMA to reduce costs, but they restrict their methods to specific tasks or network architectures. As a result, LMA remains impractical for training general large-scale neural networks. In this paper, we propose LeMA, a distributed LMA algorithm for large-scale neural network training on multi-GPU platforms. Our contributions are twofold: First, an exact dual formulation of LMA removes the memory dependence on the parameter dimension. Second, a Jacobian sharding strategy computes Jacobian shards on the fly and in parallel to avoid materializing the full Jacobian. For large-scale neural networks, LeMA reduces the memory footprint of LMA from quadratic in the number of parameters to quadratic in the batch size. This makes exact LMA steps feasible for billion-parameter models without approximate PCG solves. Furthermore, for a convolutional neural network with 1,000,022,632 parameters on an 8-GPU node, LeMA achieves a 7.97x speedup over a single GPU, corresponding to a 99.7% strong scaling efficiency.

title: Layer Engineering of Quantum Organic–Inorganic Superlattices by Thermodynamic Design
abstract: Quantum organic–inorganic superlattices, constructed by vertically stacking two-dimensional inorganic crystals and organic molecular layers, offer a powerful platform for encoding emergent electronic states through an interfacial design. However, the precise layer engineering of such hybrid architectures, particularly the deterministic control over vertical stacking periodicities, has remained elusive because of the absence of a predictive thermodynamic framework governing the staging effect in hybrid systems.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Electrochemical Molecular Dynamics within the Finite-Field Framework
abstract: Electrochemical processes at charged interfaces lie at the heart of modern technologies and their continued improvement depends on insights into the relevant atomistic processes. However, the necessary tools to impose constant-voltage conditions in molecular dynamics (MD) simulations typically directly target the electrode charge, making their extension to methods that go beyond an empirical description of metals more cumbersome. In this work, we propose an MD protocol to realize a thermodynamic ensemble in which voltage control is attained, but which is formulated purely within the framework of finite-field simulations in 3D periodic boundary conditions. We show a derivation and implementation of such a control device, which we coin an electrostat, in the ELECTRODE package within LAMMPS. Our simulations systematically benchmark the derived theory against other established approaches, for example, showing its equivalence to a potentiostat, and quantify the importance of properly accounting for ensemble fluctuations. We find that for systems of several thousands of atoms, one obtains the same equilibrium properties with the electrostat as with a simpler constant-field simulation. The difference between the two methods only manifests itself at smaller length scales, thereby establishing practical limits for the inclusion of voltage fluctuations in atomistic simulations of electrochemical systems. The strength of this framework also lies in its simplicity of extension to first-principles ab initio and reactive machine-learning potentials.

title: The effect of oxygen on the surface tension of AlTi metallic alloys
abstract: We perform molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of AlTi metallic alloy melts, with a specific focus on surface properties and the effect of oxygen. The simulations use a machine-learned inter- action potential (MLIP) that has recently been tested through experimental data for the statical and dynamical properties of AlTi melts in the bulk [Kato et al. (2026)]. We find that the surface- tension response to oxygen depends strongly on the AlTi composition. Element-resolved density profiles show that oxygen enrichment near the interface is accompanied by a suppression of the Al surface segregation observed in the oxygen-free liquid. The results are compared to experimental values obtained using levitation techniques in microgravity.

title: ADT: All-Atom Diffusion Tokenizer for 3D Molecular Structures
abstract: Discrete structural tokenization provides a promising route to autoregressive 3D molecular generation. Yet, existing tokenizers face a trade-off between compact representation and all-atom reconstruction: atom-level tokens preserve atomic details but produce long sequences, while compact residue-level protein tokens typically omit side-chain geometry. To overcome this limitation, we propose All-atom Diffusion Tokenizer (ADT), which decouples token granularity from reconstruction resolution. ADT uses one structural token per atom for small molecules and one token per protein residue that jointly represents backbone and side-chain geometry. To mitigate geometric distortion introduced by quantization, we leverage the generative capacity of diffusion models to recover fine-grained atomic geometry beyond deterministic decoding from discrete tokens. Extensive experiments across small molecules and proteins demonstrate that ADT achieves strong reconstruction from compact discrete representations while enabling high-quality autoregressive generation of both small molecules and all-atom protein structures. These results establish compact structural tokens as an effective discrete interface for all-atom molecular reconstruction and generation.

title: High-Density Iridium Single Atoms on Vanadium-Doped TiO2 for Electrochemical Water Oxidation Catalysis
abstract: Water oxidation in proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) uses IrO2 nanoparticles supported on corrosion-resistant TiO2. However, the low conductivity of TiO2 imposes electronic transport limitations that necessitate high Ir loadings for effective catalysis. Here, we present a catalyst design strategy that couples a heavily V-doped TiO2 support with high-density Ir single atoms, enabling water oxidation at minimal Ir loading. In this design, Ti-site-substituted V provides n-type doping, and selective V leaching creates cation vacancies that anchor Ir as isolated atoms.

title: Accelerated Zeolite Defect Healing Suppresses Oxygen-Containing Species Trapping for Tandem Propene Epoxidation
abstract: Selective oxidation of chemical feedstocks with in situ-generated H2O2 offers a sustainable route to high-value oxygenates, yet such tandem catalysis is often fundamentally limited by the trapping of oxygen-containing species, including H2O2-derived intermediates and oxygenated products in zeolite microenvironments, where they undergo nonproductive decomposition and side reactions. Herein, we overcome this limitation by accelerating titanosilicalite hydroxyl defect healing through intensified nucleation and subsequent accelerated crystal growth. The resulting defect-healed microenvironment facilitates the transport of in situ-generated H2O2 between bifunctional active sites while suppressing its nonproductive decomposition to H2O. Moreover, it accelerates product propylene oxide (PO) desorption by weakening hydrogen bond interactions between PO and hydroxyl defects, thereby suppressing ring-opening and overoxidation side reactions. Consequently, the defect-healed Au/TS-1 catalyst exhibits a 1.8-fold enhancement in the PO formation rate and a 2.1-fold increase in Au-based productivity. This defect-healing strategy is broadly applicable to titanosilicates, aluminosilicates, and pure-silica zeolites and can be readily extended to a 10 L scale process, delivering reductions of 21% in production cost and 54% in carbon emissions compared with conventional TS-1 synthesis. Overall, this work establishes a sustainable, scalable, and cost-effective route for zeolite defect healing and provides a general strategy to overcome the long-standing transport-decomposition trade-off in tandem catalysis with in situ-generated H2O2.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Collateral effects of bacteriophage resistance on antibiotic sensitivity in Pseudomonas aeruginosa
abstract: Collateral effect (CEs) of phage resistance can alter antibiotic sensitivity, leading to collateral sensitivity (CS). CS of phage resistance can potentially be used to design more effective phage--antibiotic combination treatments, yet insufficient knowledge on the occurrence of such phage resistance associated CS is currently available. Here, we characterized CEs across diverse Pseudomonas aeruginosa strains, antibiotics, and phages.

title: To mix or to de-mix?: Cation-π suppresses heterogeneity in local structure and dynamics of heterotypic Condensates
abstract: Heterotypic biomolecular condensates can exhibit pronounced spatial and dynamic heterogeneity because chemically distinct components compete between self- and cross-association. Here, we use coarse-grained simulations to investigate how cation-{pi} interactions modulate this competition in condensates formed by peptides with systematic variation of hydrophobicity-to-charge ratios in binary peptide pairs.

title: Modeled Oxidative Lesions Remodel the ABCB1 Linker: A Hypothesis for Transporter Regulation
abstract: Multidrug resistance mediated by P-glycoprotein (P-gp; ABCB1) remains a major barrier to chemotherapy. Cold atmospheric plasma (CAP) has increased drug responsiveness in resistant cancer models, but the molecular link between plasma-derived oxidative chemistry and ABCB1 regulation remains unresolved. We investigated whether site-specific oxidative lesions remodel the intrinsically disordered linker connecting nucleotide-binding domain 1 to transmembrane domain 2.

title: Comprehensive In Silico Design, Thermodynamic Optimization, and Dynamic Immunological Profiling of a Recombinant Multi-Epitope Vaccine Candidate Against Chandipura Virus
abstract: Chandipura virus (CHPV), an emerging arthropod-borne member of the Rhabdoviridae family, is an acute neurotropic pathogen responsible for explosive outbreaks of acute encephalitis syndrome (AES) predominantly in pediatric cohorts. With mortality rates exceeding 70%, the infection rapidly progresses to brain swelling, seizures, and death within 24 to 48 hours. The complete lack of approved antiviral therapies or preventive vaccines makes this a severe global health threat.

title: GAT1508, a selective neuronal GIRK1/2 activator, exhibits superior antiepileptic efficacy and synergizes with cannabidiol
abstract: G protein-gated inwardly rectifying potassium (GIRK; Kir3) channels are key regulators of neuronal excitability and represent promising therapeutic targets for epilepsy. Here, we characterize GAT1508, a urea-based small-molecule activator selectively targeting neuronal GIRK1/2 heterotetramers, and compare its efficacy with previously described urea compounds ML297 and GiGA1. In a pentylenetetrazole (PTZ)-induced seizure model, GAT1508 demonstrated robust antiseizure activity, outperforming both ML297 and GiGA1 and achieving efficacy comparable to valproic acid.

title: Stereochemical preorganization directs triple-helical assembly of Au4 nanoclusters
abstract: Translating local stereochemical information into higher-order helical architectures is a central challenge in materials design. Now it has been shown that stereochemically preorganized Au4 nanoclusters assemble into homochiral triple helices through directional aurophilic interactions, providing a design strategy for chiral nanocluster materials with amplified chiroptical responses.

title: Termination-dependent surface Fermiology in the intercalated altermagnet CoNb$_4$Se$_8$
abstract: Altermagnets have recently gained attention for hosting symmetry-enforced spin-split bands despite zero net magnetization. Angle-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy (ARPES) offers direct access to their electronic structure. However, the intrinsic surface sensitivity of this technique complicates the identification of the observed features: Surface states can be misinterpreted as the spin-split counterpart of bulk bands. This issue becomes particularly relevant for layered intercalated systems, where micrometer-sized domains with distinct terminations often coexist on a cleaved surface. We discuss this scenario for CoNb$_4$Se$_8$, one of the first established layered altermagnets. Supported by density functional theory calculations, we employ micro-ARPES to probe individual domains and reveal two contrasting surface terminations. We identify Co- and Se-terminated domains with characteristic surface states arising from bulk-surface connectivity of the material. Our work shows that termination-dependent surface contributions are essential for the reliable spectroscopic identification of altermagnetism and for assessing its presence across the family of layered materials.

title: Decoding CBM2 binding modes: how similar folds achieve distinct substrate preferences
abstract: Understanding the mechanisms underlying substrate recognition and selectivity is essential for developing new biotechnological applications of carbohydrate-binding modules (CBMs). Many members of CBM family 2 (CBM2) prefer binding to crystalline substrates and show diverse substrate specificities despite sharing similar folds. We show here that CBM2 specificity cannot be rationalized solely based on sequence and fold. Rather, specific binding of CBM2s to crystalline surfaces depends on a balance of topological complementarity, hydrophobic dehydration, and hydrogen-bonding interactions. We compare the binding modes of ScCBM2 and BaCBM2 on cellulose, chitin, and polyethylene terephthalate (PET) with respect to protein and substrate properties. Using MD simulations and NMR, we explore the CBMs' surface topology, hydration, solvent accessibility, and electrostatics. The results indicate that the two CBMs may bind to crystalline substrates in opposite orientations, and that the interplay between hydrophobic and {pi}-stacking interactions along the aromatic triad and hydrogen-bonding interactions on either side determines their orientation. We further show that higher water density at the aromatic triad correlates with higher substrate affinity. Lastly, we probe the interaction dynamics of BaCBM2 with PET nanoparticles and the monomer bis(2-hydroxyethyl) terephthalate (BHET) using NMR relaxation and solvent paramagnetic relaxation enhancement (sPRE) experiments, revealing a mixture of transient, low-population states involved in PET binding. These insights clarify the interplay among factors that drive CBM2 substrate recognition and highlight the importance of evaluating surface hydration and protein dynamics in future CBM2 studies.

title: Liquid hydrocarbon separation membranes: mechanistic insight, material design and microenvironment engineering
abstract: Liquid hydrocarbon separation is in great demand in the modern petrochemical industry. Membrane-based liquid hydrocarbon separation has emerged as a next-generation technology with great potential to address energy and environmental challenges, representing one of the most rapidly evolving and demanding frontiers. Despite its promise to revolutionize energy-intensive processes, practical application remains hindered by the complexity of liquid hydrocarbon mixtures and the stringent requirements on membrane materials.

title: Nano-Enabled Molecular Surveillance of Plant Health: Emerging Biosensors for Stress and Disease Detection
abstract: Plant health is a fundamental factor that determines agricultural productivity. Climate change has dramatically intensified both biotic and abiotic stresses affecting crops, leading to reduced crop quality and yield. Furthermore, traditional diagnostics often reveal stress only after visual indicators are present and irreversible damage has occurred. Culture-based techniques and molecular methods such as PCR and ELISA are precise, but they are oftentimes laborious, requiring complex equipment and may not be highly sensitive or specific.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Drug Discovery: A PRISMA-Based Systematic Review of Methods, Challenges, Taxonomy, and Evaluation Practices
abstract: This systematic review made a bold attempt to examine artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) applications in drug discovery, addressing a fragmented literature characterized by inconsistent terminology and limited benchmarking. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, Scopus, PubMed, and Web of Science were queried (January 2019-August 2026). The three databases returned 23,404 records; after removing 4,491 duplicates and multi-stage screening, 618 peer-reviewed studies were included.

title: Dynamics and Structure of Room Temperature Ionic Liquids: Ultrafast IR Experiments and MD Simulations of the Ion Cage Model
abstract: Dynamics in room-temperature ionic liquids (ILs) and the solvation of charged and neutral molecules are important to applications of ILs in battery technology, organic synthesis, and many other areas. Using ultrafast IR spectroscopy, pulse-field-gradient (pfg) NMR, and MD simulations, we investigated three ionic liquids that share the same cation but differ in their anions. IR polarization-selective pump-probe and 2D IR experiments were performed on a negatively charged probe, thiocyanate, to investigate IL dynamics. It was found that thiocyanate is an excellent surrogate for the IL anions.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Catalytic Asymmetric Allylic Substitution with Alkynylogous Silyl Enol Ethers En Route to Chiral Allenes
abstract: Despite their potential as building blocks of allenes, alkynylogous enol silanes have rarely been employed in organic synthesis. Herein, we establish their utility as nucleophiles in catalytic asymmetric allylic substitution, which results in skipped enallenes bearing two vicinal stereogenic elements (axial and central chirality). This iridium-catalyzed reaction utilizes α-alkynyl silyl enol ethers as alkynylogous nucleophile for reaction with easily accessible racemic branched allylic alcohols and endows tetrasubstituted axially chiral allenones, bearing a δ-stereocenter exclusively as a…

title: De novo design of metalloenzymes using Metal Mer
abstract: De novo enzyme design provides a route to create biocatalysts for target reactions, yet achieving high activity and selectivity directly from computation remains challenging. How best to design catalytic sites remains an open question, and enzyme design-metalloenzyme design for new-to-nature transformations in particular-is still limited in success rate, in substrate scope, and in the range of reactions accessible. Here we present a pipeline that produces efficient metalloenzymes directly from computation.

title: An Integrated Computational-Experimental Workflow for Fungal Peroxygenase Discovery and Enzyme–Substrate Prediction
abstract: Recent advances in enzyme informatics have produced increasingly powerful general models for the prediction of protein function prediction. However, their performance remains limited for underexplored enzyme families where experimental data are scarce and heterologous expression remains challenging. Here, we present a computational-experimental workflow for prioritizing, characterizing, and modeling fungal unspecific peroxygenases (UPOs) as a case study in enzyme discovery under data-limited conditions.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Monolayer van der Waals kagome lattice for high-temperature flat-band physics
abstract: Kagome lattice materials host a remarkably rich landscape of novel quantum phenomena, all arising from the intrinsic interplay of topology, correlation, and frustration. While previous studies have been mostly limited to bulk three-dimensional (3D) kagome crystals, the realization of a true two-dimensional (2D) kagome system has remained a long-standing goal, to unlock fundamentally new physics and engineering pathways inaccessible in 3D systems. In this work, we establish the first ideal 2D monolayer kagome lattices by leveraging a novel and versatile van der Waals (vdW) kagome family, A2T3X4 (A = K, Rb, Cs; T = Ni, Pd, Pt; X = S, Se). Our nano-focused angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (nano-ARPES) directly characterizes the electronic structure of A2T3X4 down to the monolayer limit, notably revealing an isolated kagome-derived flat band just below the Fermi level. Via gate-engineering of 2D A2T3X4, the kagome flat band can be further tuned to the Fermi level, allowing direct access to the partially filled flat band physics and establishing a qualitatively new 2D flat band platform. Compared to existing moire-based artificial flat band systems, this vdW kagome-based intrinsic flat band system realizes more than 220 times higher flat band electron density, opening an entirely new density and energy regime for exploring 2D flat band physics. Harnessing this high-electron-density flat band in 2D vdW kagome system provides a clear pathway to scale emergent flat band phenomena - such as fractional quantum anomalous Hall states - to far higher temperatures than currently achievable, as long-envisioned in theory and further supported by our many-body calculations.

title: Editorial: The innovative molecules emerging from Asia
abstract: Biotechs in the US and Europe face challenges, but as a recent panel discussion made clear, the competition offers global benefits

title: Mousanes scurry into the medicinal chemist’s toolbox
abstract: Serially spiro-fused cyclobutanes could be a new motif for drugmakers

title: Glowing liquids could help protect products from counterfeiters using distinctive ultraviolet light signatures
abstract: Researchers at Nottingham Trent University have developed room-temperature liquids containing chemical elements that produce distinctive patterns of light. They say the materials could provide a flexible new approach to optical tagging and anti-counterfeiting, while being compatible with existing processing and printing technologies.

title: Machine Learning Identifies an Information-Sufficiency Regime for Critical-Mineral Recovery
abstract: The recovery of critical minerals from spent lithium-ion batteries is governed by coupled feedstock chemistry, solvent composition, and processing conditions, yet heterogeneous experimental reporting makes it difficult to determine which information is essential for reliable prediction across heterogeneous experimental systems. Here, using deep eutectic solvent-based recovery as a representative resource recovery platform, we curate 814 experimental observations from 38 publications and develop an interpretable machine learning framework to identify an informationsufficiency regime.

title: Breaking the Potency Barrier: A Practical Recipe for QSAR Extrapolation
abstract: Predicting compounds that are more potent than those represented in the training data remains a difficult and practically important problem for quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) modeling. This challenge is particularly relevant during lead optimization, where the goal is to design or identify analogs that are more potent than compounds already measured. To address this problem, we developed a new Pairwise-Difference QSAR (PD-QSAR) approach that learns changes in biological activity from differences in molecular descriptors between compound pairs.

title: Programmable Formic Acid Decomposition in Flow on an Interdigitated Internal Catalytic Condenser Beyond the Sabatier Limit
Central Atom Driven Modulation of Electron Transfer in Alkyne-Protected Ag 14 Nanoclusters
abstract: Single-atom doping at the cluster core is an effective strategy for modulating the molecule-like properties of monolayer-protected nanoclusters. In this study, we systematically synthesized a pair of alkyne-protected silver nanoclusters, in which the central template anion of one nanocluster was replaced by a copper atom in the other. Incorporation of copper significantly quenched the photoluminescence of the nanocluster while enhancing its electron-transfer capability through modification of the electronic structure.

title: How to tame your bromine: bandgap tuning of solvent-free hybrid perovskites in a vapor transport deposition process
abstract: We present a sequential physical vapor and gas phase transport deposition process for batchcapable formation of metal halide perovskite films, applicable to single- and multi-junction solar cells. After evaporating porous Cs-containing Pb halides via physical vapor deposition onto the substrate or bottom cell, we use a quartz furnace to deposit the organic precursor, formamidinium iodide (FAI), onto this inorganic scaffold via vapor transport deposition. Ammonia is used as carrier gas to prevent decomposition of FAI. The resulting perovskite is already present in the photoactive alpha phase.

title: Ring Opening of Oxiranes with Amines Using Iodolium Salts as XB-Precatalysts
abstract: Herein, we report the nucleophilic ring-opening of oxiranes with substituted amines using N-heterocycle-substituted iodolium salts (NHISs) as Lewis acid pre-catalysts. Using the ring-opening of styrene oxide by aniline as a model reaction, we demonstrate that NHISs enable efficient β-aminoalcohol formation at room temperature and with pre-catalyst loadings as low as 2.5 mol%. The optimized protocol was successfully applied to a broad range of substituted oxiranes and amines, affording the corresponding β-aminoalcohols in isolated yields of up to 98%.

title: Molybdenum and Tungsten Dinitrogen Complexes Supported by Modified pentaPod Ligands: Implications on the Activation of N2 and its Conversion to NH3
abstract: The pentaPod (pentadentate tetrapodal phosphine) ligand P5R with PMe2 or phospholane (Pln) donors offers the opportunity to investigate how small changes in the ligand framework affect the properties of the corresponding transition-metal complexes. Here, we examine the influence of replacing the propyl with ethyl groups in the trident part of the pentaPod ligand with regard to N2 activation as well as N2-to-NH3 conversion by the corresponding Mo(0)N2 and W(0)N2 complexes.

title: RetroMol: Knowledge Distillation of Energy-Based Retrosynthesis Models
abstract: Retrosynthesis prediction is a central task in computer-aided synthesis planning, and synthesizability remains a persistent bottleneck in AI-driven molecular and materials discovery. We introduce RetroMol, a family of compact text-based models that transfers an energy-based critic’s ranking of candidate reactant sets into the generator itself. RetroBase, an 11M-parameter transformer encoderdecoder trained on two-reactant USPTO reactions, achieves Top-1 and Top-5 accuracies of 46.8% and 67.8% on a held-out test split.

title: TAPERSS-MoCa: A Physics-Based Monte Carlo Framework for 3D RNA Structure Prediction from Sequence
abstract: Ribonucleic acid (RNA) function is intrinsically linked to its three-dimensional architecture, yet experimental structure determination remains challenging. Here, we introduce TAPERSS-MoCa (Theoretical Analyses, Prediction, and Evaluation of RNA Structures from Sequence using a Monte-Carlo Simulator), a physics-based fragment assembly framework for predicting RNA tertiary structures directly from sequence.

title: Compartmentalized Microgels with Programmed Acoustic Anisotropy for Orthogonal Ultrasound-Triggered Motion and Cargo Release
abstract: Compartmentalization is a fundamental organizational principle in nature, enabling anisotropy required for controlled locomotion and spatiotemporal regulation of biological processes. Inspired by this principle, we present a one-step strategy to fabricate compartmentalized anisotropic microgels via liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) in aqueous droplets. Upon sodium chloride addition, concentrated N-isopropylacrylamide (NIPAAm) solutions spontaneously separate into NIPAAm-rich and NIPAAm-poor phases.

title: Genome Mining-Guided Discovery of Polyketide-Tropolone Hybrids Reveals Their Biosynthetic Logic and Antitumor Activity
abstract: 2 ABSTRACT: Tropolone-containing natural products display diverse biological activities, yet characterized fungal tropolone hybrids are dominated by sesquiterpene-derived systems, leaving polyketide-tropolone hybridization largely unexplored. Here, genome mining guided by conserved tropolone biosynthetic enzymes and an unusual dual-polyketide synthase architecture led to the discovery of fusariolones A–E and semifusariolone A from Fusarium sp. WA57, defining a distinct family of fungal polyketide-tropolone hybrids.

title: Nanoscale Phase Engineering and Magnetic Property Enhancement in High-Entropy Alloy Nanoparticles by Continuous Microparticle Laser Fragmentation in Liquid
abstract: High-entropy alloy nanoparticles (HEA NPs) offer compositional and structural tunability for applications, like water splitting, H2O2 production, or magnetocaloric technologies. Therefore, the interplay between composition, structure, and functionality is of significant interest for materials´ functionality optimization. Microparticle laser fragmentation in liquid flow (MP-LFL) is an emerging scalable method for nanoalloy production, but remains underexplored for HEA NPs.

title: Ligand Protonation Tunes Hydride-Transfer Thermochemistry in an Iron Metal-Ligand Cooperative Catalyst
abstract: Cyclopentadienone iron complexes are established metal-ligand cooperative hydrogenation catalysts, yet their bifunctional reactivity complicates the independent evaluation of proton- and hydride-transfer thermodynamics. Here, room-temperature H 2 -splitting enables deconvolution of these contributions, affording a new anionic hydride with a hydricity of 39.0 kcal·mol -1 . Ligand protonation weakens hydride-donor strength by 10 kcal mol -1 , highlighting protonation-state control of reactivity in MLC catalysis.

title: Cold Plasma Induced 3D Printing of Hydrogels
abstract: Control over when and where gelation occurs is central to the fabrication of structured soft materials, yet most approaches rely on chemical additives or uniform bulk triggers. Here, we show that cold plasma provides an external, reagent-free route to spatial and temporal control over gelation in low molecular weight hydrogel systems. Plasma exposure induces a localised decrease in pH at the plasma–liquid interface, triggering self-assembly and gel formation only in the treated region.

title: Thioethers as alkyl donors in electrochemical C–O and C–N bond forming reactions
abstract: A catalyst- and fluoride-free electrochemical method for the use of readily available thioethers as alkyl donors in C-O and C-N bond formation to furnish ethers, esters, and N-alkylated products is reported. The protocol exhibits broad functional group tolerance and is compatible with structurally complex substrates. Cyclic voltammetry studies rationalize the distinct behaviour of oxygen and nitrogen nucleophiles and guide the optimization of the electrochemical conditions, enabling the formation of coupled products from starting materials with both matched and mismatched redox potentials.

title: Describing the Fluxional Dynamics of Sub-nanoscale Clusters with Markov State Modeling
abstract: Fluxionality, or the population of and interconversion between multiple structures, has long been suggested to be relevant for understanding the physical and catalytic behavior of sub-nanoscale metal clusters on an oxide support. Much of this treatment has, however, been thermodynamic, neglecting direct exploration of the timescales for interconversion between di!erent isomers.

title: Mild acid promoted bromination with H2O2/NaBr at room temperature inspired by flavin-dependent halogenase (FDH)
abstract: Bromination is an important and frequently used organic transformation. Many elegant and reliable bromination methods have been well established; however, limitations still exist, thus calling for more sustainable approaches with broader substrate scope, better selectivity, milder condition and lower cost. In this manuscript, an effective bromination method has been established utilizing low-toxic and cost-friendly carboxylic acid/NaBr/H2O2, including bromination of (hetero)arenes, decarboxylative bromination of (hetero)aryl/vinyl carboxylic acid, ipsohydroxylation-bromination of (hetero)aryl…

title: Enantiopure Telluronium Complexes through Bidentate Chalcogen Bonding: From Solid and in Solution Studies to Chiral Recognition
abstract: This work demonstrates that tetravalent telluronium salts constitute versatile chalcogen bonding (ChB) receptors for polydentate phosphine oxide ligands. A range of bidentate phosphine oxides form highly stable 1:1 complexes with telluronium salt 1BArF in solution. Multinuclear NMR spectroscopy revealed that bidentate coordination occurs through simultaneous interaction of the two phosphine oxide groups with the telluronium centre, while variable-temperature experiments evidenced a dynamic ligand-exchange process involving the third accessible σ-hole.

title: Looking Beyond KD for Aptamer Validation: Disentangling Specific Aptamer Binding from Electrostatic Association for Basic Protein Targets
abstract: Nucleic acid aptamers provide a simple, cost-effective alternative to antibodies for targeting biomolecular analytes from ions to large protein complexes. However, the interactions of these nucleic-acid based structures in vivo remains largely uncharacterized. Here, we report the seemingly pervasive electrostatic association between nucleic acids and high isoelectric point proteins under biological conditions. Such non-specific binding runs the risk of convoluting aptamer selection and validation, while also potentially interfering with nucleic acid-based nanotechnologies in vivo.

title: Site-Selective Gaussian Accelerated Molecular Dynamics and Its Integration with Replica-Exchange Methods
abstract: We developed site-selective Gaussian accelerated molecular dynamics (ssGaMD), which selectively enhances molecular motions associated with a specified region or set of interactions. The method allows selected dihedral, electrostatic, and Lennard–Jones energy terms to be biased independently or in combination, while limiting direct biasing of the rest of the system.

title: Optical Design of Low-Haze Transparent Wood
abstract: Transparent wood (TW) composite is a structural optical material for light‑transmitting applications. TW with low haze (scattering) remains challenging due to multiple light‑scattering mechanisms at different length scales. Interfacial debonding, limited polymer accessibility in the cell wall, and refractive index (RI) mismatch between wood and polymer phases contribute to forward scattering and haze. Here we establish an optical design strategy to reduce haze/scattering in TW composites by suppressing scattering sources.

title: Spatially Encoding Fluorescence by Tailoring Clustering-Triggered Emission in Polymer Networks
abstract: Spatially programmable fluorescence has widespread potential for display, sensing and security applications, but current patterning strategies remain primarily limited to simple binary systems or methods that require locally varied chemical composition. The design of electron-rich clusters allows for a direct and facile method to induce controlled clusteroluminescence. However, achieving the necessary control over intermolecular interactions has required the design of polymers with new backbones or end groups, limiting the opportunity to spatially vary the luminescence.

title: Are Molecular Foundation Models Ready for Free Energy Simulations?
abstract: Foundation models for atomistic simulations offer broadly applicable potentialenergy surfaces that can either be applied in a zero-shot manner (without domainspecific retraining) or fine-tuned to the task at hand. Their accuracy is typically judged by energy and force errors on near-equilibrium data, yet it remains largely unclear whether these metrics translate into reliable free-energy landscapes.

title: Polymethylsilsesquioxane Aerogel-like Xerogels via a Surfactant-Free Base-Catalyzed Process
abstract: Highly insulating polymethylsilsesquioxane (PMSQ) aerogel-like xerogels were prepared from methyltrimethoxysilane in 2-propanol (IPA)/water using 10 wt % aqueous tetraethylammonium hydroxide in a one-step reaction without an acid step or surfactant. Fine interconnected skeletons were obtained after ambient-pressure drying. Infrared spectroscopy and solid-state 29Si nuclear magnetic resonance indicated fewer residual silanols in the dried material than in a two-step reference.

title: Information Dynamics Explains Chemical Reactions: A Unified Framework from NaI Photodissociation to H2 Formation
abstract: Chemical reactions are fundamentally the motion of atomic nuclei on potential energy surfaces. However, there is a methodological gap between quantum chemistry calculations and dynamical simulations: constructing potential energy surfaces is complicated, non-adiabatic couplings are difficult to treat, and different reaction types lack a unified language. In this work we introduce the information dynamics framework, reformulating chemical reactions as a three-element system: virtual space (potential energy surface rules), real space (initial wave packet data), and coupling matrix (projection…

title: DNA-programmed nanogels as dynamic membraneless compartments for synthetic cells
abstract: Bottom-up synthetic biology aims to engineer minimal systems that mimic and expand upon biological structures and functions. Programmed and dynamic organisation of intracellular components into membraneless organelles is being uncovered as vital to many cellular processes. Current approaches to introduce such membraneless compartmentalisation into bottom-up synthetic cells have focused on biomolecular coacervates, which are generally highly sensitive to environmental conditions and limited in their ability to controllably interact.

title: Probing Molecular Chirality from Vibrational to X-ray Energies in Cr(III) and Co(III) Complexes
abstract: The expression of molecular chirality across widely separated energy regimes was investigated in enantiomeric Cr(III) and Co(III) tris(trans-1,2-cyclohexanediamine) complexes using vibrational circular dichroism (VCD), electronic circular dichroism (ECD), and X-ray natural circular dichroism (XNCD), supported by single-crystal X-ray diffraction and density functional theory (DFT).

title: Systematically Constructing QM regions for Calculating QM/MM Absorption Spectra
abstract: Hybrid simulations utilizing both quantum mechanics and molecular mechanics (QM/MM) are widely used to model complex problems, such as the electronic excitation of chromophores embedded in a protein environment. Its success requires a careful choice of the portion of the system to include in the QM region to obtain accurate results. Chemical intuition and/or proximity arguments are often used to select the QM region for excited state calculations aiming to compute absorption spectra, but such choices do not guarantee accuracy.

title: The curious case of COF-300: One framework, Seventeen years of structural reinterpretation
abstract: Few frameworks have changed the meaning of their own structural description as profoundly as COF-300. Over seventeen years, this archetypal three-dimensional covalent organic framework has evolved from a powder-derived interpenetrated model into a condition-dependent structural landscape. Successive studies revealed that conserved covalent connectivity can accommodate different interpenetration states, pronounced geometrical distortion, guest-selected conformers and large-amplitude breathing through coupled linker rotation, node deformation and interframework displacement.

title: Regenerable Heterogeneous Palladium Single-Atom Catalysts for Direct C–H Arylation
abstract: Single-atom catalysts (SACs) offer tunable, recoverable heterogeneous alternatives to homogeneous metal complexes in handle-based cross-coupling reactions. However, their application to direct C–H bond functionalization remains unexplored beyond photochemical methods, as the elevated temperature and demanding reaction conditions place stringent requirements on catalyst stability. Here, we demonstrate a Pd single-atom-catalyzed C–H arylation of indoles, extending heterogeneous SACs to thermal C–H functionalization and achieving cumulative turnover numbers above 200 across five cycles. Among diverse oxygen- and nitrogen-coordinated SACs, nitrogen-coordinated sites in Pd@C3N4 uniquely combined metal retention with high activity after phosphine activation. Recycling studies coupled with in situ X-ray absorption spectroscopy reveal Pd–I bond formation as the dominant catalyst deactivation pathway. Guided by this insight, postreaction treatment in aqueous ammonia overcomes iodide poisoning, enabling catalytic activity over multiple cycles. These findings establish design principles for balancing activity, stability, and regenerability in Pd SACs for demanding C–H functionalizations, advancing their potential for greener, more step-efficient chemical synthesis.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: HEXB as a Candidate Target Gene in Keloid Radiotherapy: Based on Multi-Omics Analysis and Mendelian Randomization
abstract: IntroductionKeloid is a common and treatment-refractory conditions in plastic surgery and dermatology. Although radiotherapy for keloid has attracted increasing attention in recent years, its mechanism at the genetic level remains poorly characterized. This study investigated the relationship between radiation-related genes (RRGs) and keloid through an integrated multi-omics and machine learning framework, and to explore potential therapeutic agents targeting the identified key gene.MethodsSingle-cell RNA sequencing and multiple Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) datasets were integrated to investigate the association between RRGs and keloid. Multiple machine learning algorithms were applied to assess potential causal relationships, followed by Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis to investigate potential relationships. Spatial transcriptomics was employed to localize gene expression within keloid tissue, and virtual knockout analysis was performed to assess the functional role of the candidate gene in tissue architecture. Finally, molecular docking was conducted to screen potential therapeutic agents targeting HEXB, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were performed to evaluate the stability of the resulting protein-ligand complexes.ResultsHexosaminidase Subunit Beta (HEXB) was identified as a key gene. MR analysis further provided genetic evidence supporting a potential protective association between HEXB and keloid, identifying HEXB as a candidate protective gene. Spatial transcriptomics localized HEXB to the fibrotic dermal matrix with intralesional heterogeneity, while virtual knockout analysis implicated HEXB in maintaining epidermal-mesenchymal boundary integrity. Molecular docking demonstrated that HEXB predicted binding to several drugs, such as tamoxifen and estramustine, suggesting that HEXB may serve as a key target of these agents in keloid treatment.ConclusionThis study identifies HEXB as a candidate protective gene in keloid through an integrated multi-omics approach and suggests that HEXB may serve as a molecular target for potential therapeutic agents. These findings provide new directions for understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying radiotherapy in keloid and for developing targeted therapeutic strategies.

title: Synergy of Ni Nanoparticles and MoO x Species for Selective Hydrodeoxygenation of Lignin into Cycloalkanes
abstract: The selective hydrodeoxygenation of lignin as a substitute for fossil resources into aviation fuel-range cycloalkanes faces significant challenges due to its complex structure and diverse reaction pathways. Herein, we introduced MoOx species onto Ni nanoparticles-loaded Beta zeolite (Ni-0.2MoOx/Beta), which catalyzed the complete hydrodeoxygenation of lignin dimers and lignin-derived phenols into the corresponding cycloalkanes under mild conditions (200 °C, 2 MPa H2). Ni-0.2MoOx/Beta also enabled the hydrodeoxygenation of real lignin, achieving a cycloalkanes selectivity of over 83%.

title: Ga3+ Replacing of Fe3+ as a “Trojan Horse” Antimicrobial Strategy: Modeling the Process within Bacterial Catalase–Peroxidase KatG
abstract: Replacement of Fe3+ by Ga3+ has emerged as a promising “Trojan horse” antimicrobial strategy in response to the growing threat of antibiotic-resistant bacteria. Because many bacterial proteins hijack host iron to sustain essential redox processes, substitution with redox inactive Ga3+, which closely resembles Fe3+ in ionic radius but possesses only one oxidation state, can disrupt their activity. Among potential targets, bacterial catalase-peroxidase shows particular sensitivity to Fe3+/Ga3+ exchange. However, the structural determinants and thermodynamic driving forces governing this substitution remain poorly understood. Here we combine ad hoc force field development, molecular dynamics simulations, alchemical free energy calculations, and QM/MM methods to elucidate the molecular basis of Fe3+/Ga3+ exchange in the bacterial catalase-peroxidase KatG. Our simulations show that the axial coordination environment of the heme B cofactor is largely preserved upon metal substitution, while the distal ligand dynamically alternates between histidine and a coordinated water molecule. Energy decomposition analysis reveals residue specific differences in electrostatic and van der Waals interactions following metal exchange. Free energy calculations indicate that substitution of iron by gallium in the KatG active site is thermodynamically favorable. The presence of a coordinated water molecule emerges as a key structural feature in both metalated states, while distinct binding patterns contribute differently to the overall thermodynamic driving force. These results provide an atomistic description of gallium mediated metal substitution in KatG and offer mechanistic insight into gallium-based antimicrobial strategies, supporting the rational design of new iron-mimetic antibacterial agents.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Chemistry in Pictures: The tiniest glow sticks
(ImRN)2Fe: An Elusive Complex and the Limits of Its Ferrocene Analogy
abstract: The isolobal relationship between imidazolin-2-iminato and cyclopentadienyl ligands makes the iron bis(imidazolin-2-iminato) complex (Im R N) 2 Fe an attractive target as a potential ferrocene analog, yet reported efforts toward its isolation have been unsuccessful. Herein, we report the synthesis of (Im Dipp N) 2 Fe ( 1 ) by protonolysis of Fe 2 Mes 4 with Im Dipp NH, affording a linear, two-coordinate, high-spin Fe(II) complex (S = 2). Its coordinative unsaturation permits binding of THF, an aryl isocyanide, and TEMPO, affording complexes with varied geometries.

title: Geometrical Constraints Weaken a Nickel–Hydrogen Bond and Enable the Homolytic H2 Evolution Mechanism
abstract: Mechanistic studies of the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) are helping advance catalysis towards energy storage technologies based on water splitting. Homolytic H–H bondforming pathways are one of the fundamental mechanisms of HER, yet well-defined examples of bimetallic coupling in molecular HER catalysts remain extremely rare. A planar tetradentate bipyridine diphosphinite ligand (PONNOP) is reported that constrains the geometry of nickel complexes, weakening the Ni–H bond dissociation free energy and enabling H2 evolution via the homolytic pathway.

title: From Notch-Tip Stress to Mechanophore Activation - A Multiscale Study of Mechanochromic PMMA
abstract: Mechanophore-functionalized polymers enable optical readout of molecular-level stress under macroscopic deformation. Spiropyran (SP)-doped poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) provides a well-established platform for mechanochemical stress sensing, yet molecular stress fields around defined geometric stress concentrators remain largely disconnected from continuum mechanics. To bridge this gap, we develop a geometry-matched molecular dynamics (MD) and finite-element (FE) approach for PMMA containing two opposing semi-elliptical notches of systematically varied depth and width.

title: Mineralisation behaviour during heterogeneous photo-Fenton treatment of amoxicillin in a rotating Fe2O3-impregnated disc reactor: the controlling role of oxidant stoichiometry
abstract: Conventional biological treatment does not remove antibiotic residues, and in Jordan this matters more than in most places, because reclaimed effluent supplies a large share of the water used for irrigation. Heterogeneous photo-Fenton treatment is one candidate for a tertiary polishing step: the iron stays on a recoverable support, so the process avoids the sludge that homogeneous Fenton chemistry produces.

title: Symmetry-adapted perturbation theory for cavity-modified intermolecular interactions: QED-SAPT0 theory and implementation
abstract: We develop a cavity quantum electrodynamics symmetry adapted perturbation theory (QED-SAPT) formalism that directly models intermolecular interactions in quantized cavity environments. By formulating the zeroth-order problem in a coherent state basis, we define the inter-monomer perturbation as the sum of the standard Coulombic contribution and an inter-monomer dipole self energy contribution.

title: In Situ Mapping of Aqueous CO2 during the Electrochemical CO2 Reduction Reaction
abstract: Electrochemical interfaces feature dynamically evolving local reactant distributions that strongly influence catalytic behavior. In electrochemical CO 2 reduction (CO 2 RR), the low solubility and limited diffusion of CO 2 generate highly non-uniform local reaction environments near electrochemical interfaces. However, the actual spatial distribution of dissolved CO 2 within the interfacial structure under operating conditions remains poorly understood due to limited experimental visualization methods that probe interfacial structure.

title: Conformational Control and Charge Separation Dynamics in Perylene Bisimide-based Donor-Acceptor Polymers
abstract: The development of organic electronic materials is fundamentally influenced by the electronic structure of π-conjugated polymers. Precise positioning of donor and acceptor (D-A) units plays a crucial role in tailoring electronic properties to meet desired requirements. In this study, we report the synthesis and investigation of a novel class of D-A polymers. Four polymers, two with hanging and two with linear configurations of perylene bisimide, were designed and synthesized using Hay-Glaser and oxidative coupling polymerization methods.

title: HFO-1234yf as a Source of the 3,3-Difluoropropynyl Group
abstract: Dimethyl(phenyl)(2,3,3-trifluoroallyl)silane, the defluorosilylation product of HFO-1234yf, reacts with KHMDS to form 3,3-difluoro-1-dimethyl(phenyl)silylpropyne. The mechanism of this transformation was rationalized through DFT calculations. Deprotonation and subsequent β-fluoride elimination leads to an allene intermediate. A base-catalyzed 1,3-proton migration from the allene then results in the difluoromethylated alkyne product.

title: 3H-1,5-Benzodiazepine Derivatives as Novel Antimalarial Agents: Synthesis, Biological Evaluation and Computational Target Exploration
abstract: Malaria remains a major global health challenge worldwide and the emergence of resistance to frontline antimalarial drugs, including artemisinin-based combination therapies, underscores the need for novel antimalarial agents with distinct mechanism of action. Herein, eighteen novel 3H-1,5-benzodiazepine derivatives (5a-r) were synthesized and evaluated against chloroquine-sensitive (PfD10) and chloroquine resistant (PfW2) strains of Plasmodium falciparum. Cytotoxicity was assessed against human hepatocellular carcinoma (HepG2) cells to determine preliminary selectivity.

title: New alloy design strategy combines strength and ductility by timing hardening mechanisms
abstract: Structural metals used in engineering projects are expected to have both high strength and high ductility: the ability to withstand heavy loads and deform before failure. Achieving both of these properties at the same time, however, is challenging.

title: Reinforcement Learning for Molecule Design: A Taxonomy of Algorithms, Benchmarks, and Road to Synthesizable Leads
abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has been in the forefront in traversing the vast chemical space for novel drug discovery. In this survey, we discuss the landscape of applying RL in two related paradigms: de novo drug design, the process of generating novel drugs from scratch and drug structure optimization, an approach to enhance the drug-likeness of an existing drug, with a case study for the latter.We describe the field along a taxonomy spanning value-based, policy-gradient, reward-proportional, and search-based methods, highlighting how molecular representation methods have evolved from…

title: Acquisition Function-Guided Generation for Bayesian Optimization over Discrete Spaces
abstract: Bayesian optimization (BO) over discrete spaces is challenging due to missing gradients and the sparsity of valid solutions. Latent-space BO sidesteps both issues by fitting a surrogate in the latent space of a generative model, which however substantially complicates the direct incorporation of domain knowledge that is naturally expressed in the original discrete space. In this work, we instead combine a pretrained generative model with a surrogate defined directly in data space, where inductive biases such as domain-specific kernels can be readily incorporated. Rather than maximizing the acquisition function over the discrete design space, our method samples candidates from the generative model under a distribution tilted by the acquisition function. To recover useful gradients for sampling, we embed this tilted distribution into a diffusion bridge that yields a smooth, posterior-averaged acquisition function. This leads to \emph{acquisition function guided generation} (AFGG), which we instantiate with a categorical diffusion model and an autoregressive normalizing flow. Across a broad suite of molecular benchmarks, the diffusion model variant performs on par with leading BO methods, while the flow model variant outperforms state-of-the-art methods in most cases and remains highly competitive otherwise. Our implementation is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/afgg.

title: Generalized length-gauge time-dependent Liouville equation
abstract: The length-gauge (LG) time-dependent Liouville equation is a major workhorse to simulate ultrafast dynamics. The equation features the commutator between the density operator $\hatρ$ and the position operator ${\bf r}$, $\langle n{\bf k}|[{\bf r},\hatρ]|m{\bf k}'\rangle$, where $|n{\bf k}\rangle$ and $|m{\bf k}'\rangle$ are Bloch states for bands $n$ and $m$ at crystal momenta ${\bf k}$ and ${\bf k}'$, respectively. This commutator has two irreconcilable versions: Kohn and Luttinger (Phys. Rev. ${\bf 108}$, 590 (1954)) have two partial derivatives with respect to ${\bf k}$ and ${\bf k}'$, but Aversa and Sipe (AS) (Phys. Rev. B ${\bf 52}$, 14636 (1995)) have one partial derivative and one Dirac delta. For several decades, this outstanding discrepancy has received little attention. Here, we show that the generalized LG time-dependent Liouville equation has two partial derivatives, but no Dirac delta. Physically, the ${\bf k}$-off-diagonal matrix elements of the position operator provide a channel by which the electric field generates ${\bf k}$-off-diagonal matrix elements for $\hatρ$ in LG. The discrepancy emerges when the position matrix is assumed to be diagonal in ${\bf k}$. Consequently the AS' equation is a limiting case of our generalized Liouville equation, where the relative momentum ${\bf Q}$ between two states is ignored. Our numerical test reveals that the ${\bf k}$-diagonal formalism yields qualitatively different results and underestimates both energy absorption and polarization by a factor of 7. Our study establishes a general formalism for the length-gauge time-dependent Liouville equation and opens the door for future research on the ultrafast time scale, while prior results based on the ${\bf k}$-diagonal only equation may need to be revisited.

title: CASyM: Chemotype Annotation through Synthesis Mapping
abstract: The identification and annotation of chemotypes is central to structure–activity relationship studies and property optimization in drug discovery. Current computational approaches rely on predefined fragmentation rules or structural similarity to identify these molecular scaffolds, often overlooking the rich information available in reaction data. Here, we introduce CASyM (Chemotype Annotation through Synthesis Mapping), a novel approach that leverages hierarchical reaction data to systematically identify chemotypes within compound libraries. CASyM constructs synthesis graphs from curated reaction data sets, detects major common intermediates, and builds chemotype graphs that capture the hierarchical and interconnected nature of chemical synthesis. SMARTS patterns are extracted to define chemotypes, enabling robust assignment of target molecules, including those absent from the original reaction data. We demonstrate the approach across three case studies using public patent data, proprietary electronic laboratory notebook data from drug discovery projects, and simulated multistep synthesis data for compounds lacking experimental synthesis records. CASyM achieves high coverage of target molecules (85–99%), reveals chemotype-property relationships, and enables chemotype assignment in the absence of experimental data. This reaction-centric approach provides a powerful framework for chemotype annotation, facilitating series exploration and optimization in medicinal chemistry.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Freshwater Blackworms Solving a Maze
abstract: We investigated the behaviour of freshwater blackworms (\emph{Lumbriculus variegatus}) in a circular maze containing food in its central chamber. Analysis of 11 time-lapse recordings showed that all tested worms entered the central chamber, although first-arrival times and spatial exploration patterns varied substantially. Registered occupancy maps revealed non-uniform use of corridors and chambers. Because the study did not include a no-food control, the observations demonstrate central-chamber entry and spatial exploration but do not by themselves establish food localisation or chemotaxis.

title: Isomer-resolved ion-molecule reaction kinetics of HCO+ and HOC+
abstract: The HCO$^+$/HOC$^+$ abundance ratio has been observed to vary significantly in different astrophysical environments, making it an important diagnostic tool for exploring the interstellar medium. However, uncertainties in the reaction rates and branching ratios of key chemical reactions involving these ions affect the conclusions drawn from observations of either these species or other species that are derived on their basis. Here, we present isomer-resolved ion-molecule reaction rate coefficients of reactions involving HCO$^+$ and HOC$^+$ using a cryogenic ion trap experiment. We measured the rate coefficients of the isomerization reaction of HOC$^+$ to HCO$^+$ with H$_2$ and CO, as well as three different reactions producing both isomers: CO$^+$ + H$_2$ , H$_3^+$ + CO, and ArH$^+$ + CO. Our results show that the reaction of CO$^+$ with H$_2$ predominantly produces HCO$^+$ with a negligible yield of HOC$^+$ . This result is in agreement with recent theoretical predictions, but in major contrast to the generally accepted branching ratio based on previous experimental results. We also find that the isomerization reaction of HOC$^+$ to HCO$^+$ is efficient with both H2 and CO. We were able to assess the impact of our new measured reaction rate coefficients on the predicted HCO$^+$/HOC$^+$ abundance ratio using a state-of-the-art astrochemical model.

title: Enantioselective Coupling of Unactivated Alkenes with α-Imino Esters via Alkylzirconium Radical Intermediates
abstract: Converting simple hydrocarbon feedstocks into stereochemically complex molecules remains a central goal of synthetic chemistry. α-Tetrasubstituted amino acids, which feature densely substituted stereogenic centers and important applications in chemical biology and medicinal chemistry, are particularly challenging to access through direct catalytic methods. Here, we report a photoinduced nickel-catalyzed asymmetric alkylation of α-imino esters using alkylzirconium intermediates generated directly from unactivated alkenes.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Coupling Raman Spectroscopy and Acoustic Microscopy to Characterize Glioblastoma Resistance
abstract: Therapy resistance in glioblastoma is usually described in genetic or metabolic terms. Here we ask whether it also has a measurable biophysical form.
